title: Mistral ships 1T-parameter Large 4 — open weights that 'only defend'
summary: Mistral Large 4 arrives with a trillion parameters, a top cyber score, and a promise that its open weights will be used to defend but not attack — Ada and Alan argue whether open weights can be gated at all, against Anthropic's new tiered cyber access. Then the Florida woman arrested after Claude flagged her messages, what happens between typing and a referral, and TIME's look inside Meta Muse's hourly dossiers.

topics: Mistral Large 4 ('Le Chonk'): 1T total / 49B active parameters, natively multimodal, trained from scratch on 3,800 Nvidia Grace Blackwell GPUs in Mistral's European data centers (TechCrunch: 4,000); preview API at $1.36/$4.18 per million tokens, weights end of October after safety testing; Artificial Analysis 38 vs Mistral Large 3's 9 (Willison: ~6 months behind the frontier, not Fable-class); reasoning only 'none' or 'high', with Willison's high-reasoning pelican using fewer tokens (2,717 vs 3,275); vendor-reported 82% on AA cyber index vulnerability reproduction (highest tested) and 93% Cybench; optimized for cybersecurity, finance and chip design with ASML and Samsung as lead investors; Pierre Stock's pledge that open weights will be used 'to defend' via trusted partners and governments. On-air argument: open weights keep training-time safety but lose the access gate, and refusals can be trained out; contrasted with Anthropic's three-tier Cyber Verification Program (Defense / Red Team orgs-only / Specialized with US government; 129,000+ verified vulnerabilities, 33,000+ critical or high) and Nathan Lambert's 'Open Unsafe, Closed Unsafe'. Unresolved: Alan holds where the model runs matters more than the score (defenders who cannot call an API); Ada holds the gate is the only control we know how to build.

Florida (Bonita Springs) woman arrested after Anthropic flagged Claude messages threatening the Lee County Sheriff's Office (Sept 26 and 27; second mentions a new gun); charged with written threats, a second-degree felony; the sheriff's 'uses Claude like a diary'. Taught: the monitoring pipeline as classifier trade-off, human review, then a policy threshold — Gizmodo's quoted 'imminent physical harm or death' emergency standard versus the privacy policy's broader 'prevent serious harm' language, flagged content de-identified for classifier training but re-identifiable for enforcement; diary vs letter vs privileged conversation and the therapist duty-to-warn contrast. Paired with TIME's finding that Meta Muse updates hourly 'dossiers on you and the people you've mentioned' (~4M users). Unresolved: Alan holds Muse is the bigger story; Ada holds the Florida case is the template every assistant will need.

dives.story: Mistral Large 4 and whether open weights can only defend
dives.why_it_matters: Security teams and governments choosing an open model need to know that a vendor's 'defend, not attack' pledge cannot bind weights once released, while the model leads a cyber benchmark.

dives.story: The Claude 'diary' arrest and the monitoring pipeline
dives.why_it_matters: Anyone who confides in a chatbot is writing to a reader with a referral policy, and the threshold lives on a web page rather than in law.

lore.note: Ada staked out that providers should publish annual law-enforcement referral counts, how many flags human reviewers cleared, and the referral threshold in plain language at the point of typing — 'in this story I'm the diary', and people should know who else is in the room. Not settled.
